scope: Sargent and Stachurski, Dynamic Programming, Volume 1 (Finite States), Chapter 6: Stochastic Discounting. The spectral radius, Neumann series and Perron-Frobenius theorem on a general finite state space, including the irreducible case (positive and unique eigenvectors, the unique positive stationary distribution of an irreducible Markov matrix) and the everywhere-positive case with the convergence rho(A)^(-t) A^t -> e eps^T deferred from Chapter 2; lifetime valuation with time-varying discount factors (Theorem 6.1.1), the spectral radius via expected discount factors (Lemma 6.1.2), discounting that depends on a component of the state (Lemma 6.1.3), necessity of the spectral radius condition (Lemma 6.1.4); eventual contractions (Theorem 6.1.5, Propositions 6.1.6-6.1.7); MDPs with state-dependent discounting, Lemma 6.2.1 and Proposition 6.2.2 on optimality, the HPI and OPI steps, convergence of value function iteration under a dominating discount operator; exogenous discounting (Proposition 6.2.3) with convergent VFI; the inventory model with time-varying interest rates; Markov asset pricing of stationary and growing dividend streams with the Lucas SDF and Gaussian shocks; the Harrison-Kreps pricing operator; and the provable exercises.
source: Thomas J. Sargent and John Stachurski, Dynamic Programming, Volume 1: Finite States, Chapter 6, pp. 182-212; Theorem 2.3.1, p. 69.
